newsitem.title: USA: Sun Co to keep Marcus Hook unit down.
newsitem.headline: Sun Co to keep Marcus Hook unit down.

text.p: Sun Co Inc said Friday it plans to keep shut the crude distillation unit at its Marcus Hook, Penn., refinery for another 26 days for economic reasons.
The company said weak prices for gasoil, which is used in the refinery's catalytic cracker -- also currently down for maintenance -- made it uneconomical to sell the product on the market.
The 80,000 barrel per day crude unit was pulled off line on Oct. 4 for what was originally an 18-day scheduled maintenance, said company spokesman Bud Davis.
The maintenance coincided with a 44-day turnaround at the 85,000 bpd catalytic cracking unit. The crude unit fed the cracker gasoil to produce gasoline.
"Our plan was to bring the (crude) unit up after 18 days and we were going to sell gasoil (heating oil) on the market but the margins on gasoil versus crude oil don't justify running it," said Davis.
Since peaking in early October, heating oil-to-crude margins have slumped by around $3.30 to $4.50 on a per barrel basis. This level makes it uneconomical to run the unit, Davis said.
Last week, Sun Co reported an $8 million operating loss for the third quarter and said its Northeast Refining Ltd unit, which includes the Marcus Hook plant, lost $20 million in the quarter.

The division ran at 100 percent of rated capacity -- averaging inputs of over 481,000 barrels daily -- but was hit by the high cost of crude and relatively low products prices, Sun chairman and chief executive Robert Campbell said of last week's results.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1620
